column3: Close to the Greek.

NASB supplies “some” and “Jesus”; “for every cause” is rendered “for any reason at all.”
NASB adds “them” after “created” and prints the quotation in capitals.
Close to the Greek; the quotation is in capitals.
NASB renders “man” as “no man.”
NASB renders “roll of divorce” as “certificate of divorce” and prints the Old Testament wording in capitals.
“It was not this way” is rendered “it has not been this way.”
NASB follows the critical text: it ends at “commits adultery” and lacks the Textus Receptus clause about marrying a divorced woman. “Sexual immorality” is rendered “immorality.”
NASB renders “the case” as “the relationship” and places “not” with “to marry.”
NASB renders “receive” as “can accept” and adds “men.”

NASB adds “some” and renders “little children” as “children.”
“Permit” is rendered “let … alone,” and “of such is” becomes “belongs to such as these.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text with “Teacher” (no “good”); “have” is rendered “obtain.” NASB omits “behold.”
NASB follows the critical text: “Why are you asking Me about what is good? There is only One who is good.” The Textus Receptus has “Why do you call Me good? No one is good except God.”
